paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the faith you hold is worth guarding. Jude urges the saints to "contend earnestly for the faith entrusted once for all to the saints" (Jude 1:3). It was handed over complete, so nobody gets to sneak in a new recipe and call it the original. That's why Jude gets loud about men who "turn the grace of our God into a license for immorality" (Jude 1:4).

Now watch HOW Jude says to contend. He doesn't tell the beloved to out-yell anybody. He says to build yourselves up in your most holy faith, pray in the Holy Spirit, and "keep yourselves in the love of God as you await the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ to bring you eternal life" (Jude 1:20-21). Even Michael, the archangel, said only "The Lord rebuke you!" when he disputed with the devil (Jude 1:9). If Michael lets the Lord handle the rebuking, I can let Him handle it too, friend.

And the fight is never only about you. Jude says to have mercy on those who doubt and to save others by snatching them from the fire (Jude 1:22-23). Then he ends on praise to the One "able to keep you from stumbling and to present you unblemished in His glorious presence, with great joy" (Jude 1:24). So hold tight to the faith, friend, but remember it's HIS hands holding you first.
